desc:
For a non-negative integer n, let e be the largest exponent such that 2e divides n!, the product 1 * 2 * ... * n (with 0! = 1). Return e.

The factorial is far too large to compute for big n, so count the factors of 2 directly.

n = 5  -> 3    (5! = 120 = 8 * 15)
n = 10 -> 8    (10! = 3628800 = 256 * 14175)
n = 0  -> 0
hints: Only the even numbers contribute factors of 2, but they contribute several each. Do not multiply the numbers out.
For each power 2<sup>i</sup>, count the multiples of 2<sup>i</sup> in 1..n. Each such multiple contributes one more factor of 2.
The total is the sum of floor(n / 2<sup>i</sup>) for i ≥ 1. This sum equals n minus the number of 1 bits in n.
editorial: A number m contributes one factor of 2 for each power 2<sup>i</sup> (i ≥ 1) that divides it. So the total exponent is the sum over i ≥ 1 of the number of multiples of 2<sup>i</sup> in [1, n], which is floor(n / 2) + floor(n / 4) + floor(n / 8) + ... (Legendre's formula).

Write n in binary. floor(n / 2<sup>i</sup>) keeps only the bits of n at positions at least i, shifted down. A bit of n at position j therefore contributes 2<sup>j-1</sup> + 2<sup>j-2</sup> + ... + 1 = 2<sup>j</sup> - 1 to the sum over all i ≥ 1. Adding over the set bits gives n minus the number of 1 bits of n.
So the answer is n - popcount(n), computed in O(log n) time with a bit count. It is also the number of trailing zero bits of n!.
